subject: Discovery recap & POC plan — structured output (JSON schema) and function/tool calling
messages:
From: Connor O'Brien <connor_obrien@redwood.ai>
To: Elena Ortiz <eortiz@finpay.com>
Cc: Maya Srinivasan <maya_srinivasan@redwood.ai>, Dev Patel <dev_patel@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 5 Mar 2026 15:02:00 -0700
Subject: Discovery recap & POC plan — structured output (JSON schema) and function/tool calling

Hi Elena —

Thanks again for the time today. Below is a short recap of what we heard and a proposed next-step plan for a lightweight POC focusing on deterministic structured output and function/tool calling for your payments reconciliation workflow. Please flag anything I missed.

Quick recap (pain points + context)
- Pain: False positives in reconciliation and manual mapping of transaction metadata across providers (time wasted reconciling ~6–8% volume).
- Current stack: Internal microservices (Node.js), Postgres for ledger, some Lambda-based enrichment steps, SFTP inbound files. No existing LLM infra.
- Goal: Produce deterministic, machine-parseable reconciliation records (JSON) and a small agent workflow that can call your enrichment microservice and produce fields expected by downstream systems.
- Success criteria (what FinPay will count as success):
  1) Schema compliance: >95% of POC outputs validate against the provided JSON schema with zero ambiguity in field semantics.
  2) Deterministic mapping: For a representative 48-hour sample, finalized outputs reduce manual reconciliation touch by at least 40%.
  3) Latency: Per-request median latency <= 400ms for calls that require no external enrichment; <= 800ms when calling enrichment service.

Proposed immediate plan (POC, ~2–3 weeks)
- Week 0 (this week): Exchange sample payloads and a minimal JSON schema (I attached a starter schema).
- Week 1: Redwood builds a small prototype that accepts your sample events, returns a validated JSON object, and demonstrates function/tool calling to a mocked enrichment endpoint.
- Week 2: Run the prototype against your 48-hour representative sample; collect validation rates, error types, and latency.
- Deliverable: A short report + reproducible harness and a recommendation for deployment mode (Hosted API vs Dedicated).

Open questions / clarifications we need from you
- Which fields must be strictly canonical (never nullable) vs optional? We marked a first-pass list in the attached example-payment-schema.json.
- Are there any PII constraints or redaction rules we should enforce at the model level or before sending payloads?
- Who from your engineering team should we loop in to provision test endpoints (API key/temporary creds)?

Attachments: finpay-discovery-notes.pdf (notes from call), example-payment-schema.json (starter schema)

Next steps / asks
- Can you confirm the primary success criteria above and reply with the two engineers we should work with to get sample payloads and test endpoints?
- I’ll follow up to propose 2 x 30-minute slots for a quick schema walkthrough with your engineers.

Thanks — feel free to reply directly or mark edits in the attached PDF.

Best,
Connor O'Brien
Senior Solutions Executive | Redwood Inference
connor_obrien@redwood.ai | +1 (415) 555-6123

--
Redwood Inference — developer-first inference runtime
From: Elena Ortiz <eortiz@finpay.com>
To: Connor O'Brien <connor_obrien@redwood.ai>
Cc: Maya Srinivasan <maya_srinivasan@redwood.ai>, Dev Patel <dev_patel@redwood.ai>, Andrew Lee <alee@finpay.com>
Date: Thu, 5 Mar 2026 16:10:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Discovery recap & POC plan — structured output (JSON schema) and function/tool calling

Connor —

Appreciate the thorough recap and the suggested timeline. That matches what we discussed. Quick responses inline:

- Canonical fields: transaction_id, settled_at, amount_minor, currency, merchant_id — these must always be present and not null. We'll provide a list in the sheet.
- PII: We must mask card_pan and full_account_number before sending to any external service. Tokenized IDs are fine.
- Test endpoints: pls coordinate with Andrew (cc'ed) — he manages our integration environment. He can provide temporary service endpoints and a service account.

A couple of notes on success criteria: the 95% schema validation threshold is fine, but for production we expect >99% with fallback rules documented. For the POC, 40% reduction in manual touch is a good milestone.

We'll send sample files (SFTP) by end of day Friday. Let us know what format you prefer (raw CSV vs normalized JSON).

Thanks,
Elena Ortiz
Head of Product Operations | FinPay
eortiz@finpay.com | +1 (212) 555-0188
